title: The composition of rotation vectors loses rotation increments below 1e-8 rad; Lie group nodes in the implicit Runge-Kutta solvers
author: Claude-JG
description: EXUlie::CompositionRotationVector (and CompositionRuleForRotationVectors of lieGroupBasics.py) takes the composed angle from x = cos(w/2) by sqrt(1 - x^2): for w below about 1e-8 rad x rounds to 1 and the angle to 0, so small rotation increments are quantized. With NodeRigidBodyRotVecLG this is the floor of 2e-10 at which the Newton iteration of LobattoIIIA4 and Radau3 stalls at small steps (the slider crank at h = 6.25e-5 fails); generalized-alpha composes with the same function. Decided (revision2026c step RG20.7.2): sin(w/2) from the vector part of the quaternion product, |rho|/2, which is the same in exact arithmetic and accurate for small angles; the tangent operator T(Delta) in the stage Jacobian of the implicit Runge-Kutta solvers, as generalized-alpha with lieGroupAddTangentOperator; a check of the stage Jacobian against finite differences at verbose level 4; the order of the rotations measured.
releaseNotes: EXUlie::CompositionRotationVector and lieGroupBasics.CompositionRuleForRotationVectors take the composed angle as 2 atan2(|rho|/2, x) from the quaternion product, instead of from x = cos(w/2) alone, which rounded rotations below about 1e-8 rad to zero; composing pi*n with itself is exact for any axis. With it the implicit Runge-Kutta solvers run with Lie group nodes at all step sizes (LobattoIIIA4 and Radau3 stalled at small steps); their stage Jacobian has the tangent operator of the rotation increment. Simulations with Lie group nodes change at the level of rounding. Verbose level 3 of the implicit Runge-Kutta solvers prints the residual per block, level 4 checks the stage Jacobian against finite differences; implicitRungeKuttaLieGroupTest.py.
